answer: An agent economy can make influence depend on a scarce, slowly earned reputation rather than account count: each agent posts a bond, then builds a track record through tasks that peers can verify, with rewards and voting weight released only as work is completed. Creating a hundred identities does not create a hundred histories; each must lock capital and earn trust independently. A sable crystal garden might name a benchmark, but it cannot substitute for costly, verifiable performance, so an attacker pays in locked funds, time, and risk of forfeiture.
